The paper presents a physico-mathematical model for determining the heat transfer parameters between viscous gasdynamic flotations and cooled gas turbine blades made using composite permeable membrane (CPM) technology.

The mathematical model includes equations of dynamic and thermal boundary layers, three-dimensional transient heat conduction in CPM cooled frames, complex hydraulic flow and cooling inside the channels of a cooled blade.
A complex problem was solved to determine the thermal state of microrocket engines, where a method was proposed for immersing a multiply-connected domain in a region of the simplest form.
The results obtained showed greater cooling efficiency at lower cooling medium costs.
The CPM has a two-layer structure with 7 different modes of cooling medium flow in the channels.
The geometric dimensions of the CPM structure are: a = 5 mm, b = 5 mm, c = 2 mm, d = 2 mm, l = 1.5 mm, f = 1.5 mm, δ1 = 0.5 mm, δ2 = 0.5 mm, δ3 = 0 mm, δ4 = 0.5 mm, δ5 = 0.5 mm, P = 0.5 mm.

The thermal and physical properties of the CPM frame materials are: λ1 = 0.5042 kW/m·K, ρ1 = 7800 kg/m^3, c1 = 1.26 kJ/kg·K for the first material, and λ2 = 0.1512 kW/m·K, ρ2 = 7800 kg/m^3, c2 = 1.26 kJ/kg·K for the second material.
The gasdynamic flotation characteristics are: Te = 1600 K, ρe = 200 m/s, Pr = 0.71, δe = 0.1 kg/m.

The cooling efficiency metric θ is defined as θ = (Te - Tw1)/(Te - Tcooled), where Te is the effective temperature of the gasdynamic flotation, Tw1 is the temperature of the impermeable wall, and Tcooled is the temperature of the cooling medium.
The results show that lower unit surface conductance on the impermeable wall leads to higher CPM cooling efficiency.
The CPM cooling technology allows for greater cooling efficiency at lower cooling medium costs, by optimizing the heat transfer parameters.
The modeling and analysis can be used to design more efficient cooling systems for high-temperature gas turbine engines.
The paper was supported by grants from the Russian Foundation for Basic Research and the President of the Russian Federation.
The authors applied the immersion method and fractional step method to numerically solve the 3D transient heat conduction problem in the multiply-connected CPM domain.
The paper presents a new economical and stable numerical method for solving spatial nonstationary heat transfer problems in multiply-connected domains.
The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the CPM cooling technology compared to traditional approaches.
